key_insight: A steric-engineered ternary-solvent strategy produces hybrid perovskite monolayers exceeding 1,000 µm² by suppressing out-of-plane stacking and promoting lateral growth.
engineering_relevance: Large ultrathin crystals enable solvent-free, shadow-mask contacts for lithography-free optoelectronics with very low static power consumption.
method: Combine alcohol cosolvents with an amine additive to suppress stacking.
Use molecular dynamics and quantum-chemical calculations to investigate solvation and growth mechanisms.
Fabricate planar devices on isolated ultrathin perovskite channels using physical shadow masks.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports synthesis across multiple spacer cations, metals, and halides; (PEA)₂PbI₄ devices achieve approximately 0.2 pW static power at 5 V, 250-fold below drop-cast films, with a light-to-dark current ratio of 430.
watch_item: Device yield, long-term stability, and reproducibility at manufacturing scale are not established in the abstract.
paper_title: Universal Synthesis of Large-Area Hybrid Perovskite Monolayers Enabling Lithography-Free, Low-Static-Power Optoelectronics
